LESSON: FRENCH ACCENT MARKS IN BRAILLE • DIPHTHON GS (AEOE)

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 8
Subject: GRADE
Strand: French Braille
Topic 9.1: French Accent marks in Braille • Diphthon gs (Aeoe)
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers French Accent marks in Braille • Diphthon gs (Aeoe), part of French Braille in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 8 GRADE.

Key inquiry question: Why is it important to use the correct accent in a French word?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. feel tactile Braille flashcards with individual accent marks (é, è, ê, ë, ç) and say their names aloud with teacher support and discuss in groups.

2. sort Braille word cards into groups based on the type of accent mark present and share with peers to counter check the correction and give feedback,

3. listen keenly to the audio word record played by the teacher and read Braille word strips with accent marks and diphthongs (école, père, Noël, cœur)

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. feel tactile Braille flashcards with individual accent marks (é, è, ê, ë, ç) and say their names aloud with teacher support and discuss in groups.
2. sort Braille word cards into groups based on the type of accent mark present and share with peers to counter check the correction and give feedback,
3. listen keenly to the audio word record played by the teacher and read Braille word strips with accent marks and diphthongs (école, père, Noël, cœur)

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on French Accent marks in Braille • Diphthon gs (Aeoe) together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Communication and Collaboration: the learners collaborate to feel tactile Braille flashcards with individual accent marks

and discuss in groups.

● Digital Literacy: the learners use Braille displays or refreshable Braille readers to read and write accented French words.

Values:
Unity: the learner respects peers’ opinion when sorting Braille word cards into groups based on the type of accent mark

present and share with peers to counter check the correction and give feedback

52

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Social Cohesion: the learners enjoy engaging in storytelling using Braille texts that emphasize correctly accented words and

diphthongs, then reflect on how meaning could change without them.
